text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing steady mem growth on streaming chat when a tool-loop keeps appending steps. Started ~2GB, after ~1h up to ~9GB and didn't reclaim. Running on prod-dedicated-01. KV cache pages climbing.
sam: do we have a heap profile? can you attach pprof / tracemalloc or heapshot?
maya: quick heapshot I grabbed:
```
Heapshot #12: totals: objects 1.2M, bytes 1.1G
Top by size:
  kv_cache_item   430MB  120k objs
  string_buffer   210MB  340k objs
  other_objs      150MB  200k objs
```
KV entries count also steadily increases in the monitoring dashboard.
richard: that matches a fragmentation + never-evicted pattern. Are we accidentally creating per-step keys instead of reusing conversation-prefix keys?
maya: looks like current code uses unique key per tool call (context_id + step_id). Expected reuse by conversation prefix. Example snippet from runtime:
```
- key = f"kv:{context_id}:{step_id}"
+ key = f"kv:{context_id}:prefix_{prefix_hash}"
```
If we hash conversation prefix we can limit key cardinality.
jen: also noticed kernel selection falling back to generic kernels when seq_len > 2048, which changes KV layout and increases allocations. Profiler shows kernel=attn_v2_generic in the long-context runs.
sam: good catch. Add a synthetic test that simulates long context + tool-loop and asserts steady-state memory. Also flip on KV_EVICT_DEBUG=1 to log eviction candidates.
ops-bot: Incident #INFR-2045 opened by maya: "kv growth in streaming chat - potential leak". Priority: P2 -> escalated.
maya: repro steps I ran locally:
1) start runtime with --max-seq 8192
2) run tools/ev_repro.py --convo-len 6000 --loop 200
3) watch RSS climb.
Logs stored: gs://redwood-artifacts/kv-leak/1765127890
richard: can you paste `cat /proc/meminfo` and `slabtop`? suspect slab fragmentation due to many small allocations.
maya: pasted key lines:
```
MemTotal:       128847556 kB
MemFree:          2345678 kB
AnonHugePages:         0 kB
Slab:           1283456 kB
```
Slab usage is high and not dropping after GC cycles.
sam: I can reproduce at smaller scale. Theory: KV entries aren't evicted because TTL/eviction is LRU but streaming holds references in the active request scope preventing eviction. Also the fallback kernel path allocates unpooled buffers.
jen: idea: use weak refs for in-flight KV pointers or introduce a per-conversation capped-keyset that reuses entries. Also consider forcing shrink after N steps but must measure hit-rate impact.
maya: perf impact: 95th latency normally ~120ms; after long stream it goes to ~420ms and hosts OOM when memory > ~90%.
richard: let's add tracing when KV entries are created vs reused (trace id + key) and an allocator counter for kv_allocs/kv_frees. Instrumentation will tell whether keys are accumulating or just leaking memory in slabs.
sam: created draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/498 (wip) — implements prefix reuse + emits eviction candidate metrics. Running unit/integration locally.
ci-bot: build #498 started. Unit tests passed; integration `test_kv_eviction` failed flaky on first run.
jen: assign INFR-2045 to eng-runtime rotation and tag @oncall. We should canary any change under lower traffic.
maya: I'll run canary with PR diff and KV_EVICT_DEBUG=1. Artifacts uploaded: /mnt/artifacts/kv-leak-1765127890.tar.gz
sam: small repro script (attached) that hits the runtime with streaming chat + tool loop; run with `python tools/ev_repro.py --convo-len 6000 --loop 200 --host localhost:8080` to reproduce mem growth.
richard: if canary doesn't reclaim within 15m post-stream, we should auto-revert. Add monitoring alert: if host mem > 85% for 10m escalate P1.
ops-bot: SLA alert threshold for host memory > 85% set to P1 for INFR-2045. Notifications to #incidents and oncall.
maya: next steps: (1) land PR with prefix reuse + unit tests, (2) run long-stream stress for 2h in staging, (3) canary to prod-dedicated-01 with debug on, (4) if stable, roll remaining hosts.
sam: I'll also check kernel-selection heuristics to avoid falling back to generic kernel when not strictly necessary; maybe change threshold from 2048 -> 4096 for some models.
jen: leaving notes in ticket about potential trade-offs (cache hit vs memory). Good progress. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks all — will update INFR-2045 after canary.
